Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 64, titled *Sayana* ("Lying down"), belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka's *sekhiya* (rules of training) section within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga. The text sets out monastic etiquette regarding lying down, and has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali tradition, direct counterparts occur in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, the Bhikkhu Parivāra, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Parallels also survive widely across non-Pali traditions, including Sarvāstivāda (extant in Chinese and Sanskrit), Mūlasarvāstivāda (in Tibetan and Sanskrit), Mahīśāsaka (in Chinese), Dharmaguptaka (in Chinese), Kāśyapīya (in Chinese), and the *Upāliparipṛcchā*.
